Done! I've set up the sync service to run automatically in the background at system startup. Here's what was created:

**Files created:**
- **sync-loop.sh** — Bash script that runs sync.sh continuously (default: every 5 minutes)
- **start-sync.bat** — Windows batch wrapper to find and run the bash script
- **setup-sync-autostart.ps1** — One-command installer for Windows Task Scheduler
- **scripts/AUTOSTART.md** — Full documentation with management commands

**To activate it, run as Administrator:**
```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser -Force
& "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w2\persist.autostart-v8-178667801612795\setup-sync-autostart.ps1"
```

Once installed, the sync service will:
- Start automatically when your computer boots
- Pull the upstream feed every 5 minutes
- Log timestamps to `data/feed.log`

**Manage with PowerShell:**
```powershell
Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncService"      # Start now
Stop-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncService"       # Stop
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "SyncService"        # Check status
```
